## Research question options

1. **Residential investment:** how has immigration affected rents and returns for landlords and investors in Spain?
2. **Construction sector:** does immigration drive new housing supply, through both demand and labour?
3. **Firms and housing:** do high housing costs make it harder for firms to attract migrant workers?

::: {.small .muted}
Barcelona or Catalonia can work as a case study within any of the three.
:::

## Literature review

::: {.refs}
González, L. and Ortega, F., 2013. [Immigration and housing booms: evidence from Spain](https://doi.org/10.1111/jors.12010). *Journal of Regional Science*, 53(1), pp.37-59.

Saiz, A., 2007. [Immigration and housing rents in American cities](https://ideas.repec.org/p/iza/izadps/dp2189.html). *Journal of Urban Economics*, 61(2), pp.345-371.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="How to read them"}
For each paper: **question, data, method, result**, and what it adds to your TFG.
:::

::: notes
These are the two readings I sent by email. González and Ortega is the Spanish benchmark; Saiz covers rents. Their references, and the papers that cite them, lead to the rest of the literature.
:::

## Possible data

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Foreign population, by province | [INE, Continuous Population Statistics](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/INEbase/es/operacion.htm?c=Estadistica_C&cid=1254736177095&menu=resultados&idp=1254735572981) |
| House prices | [INE, Housing price index](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/INEbase/operacion.htm?c=Estadistica_C&cid=1254736152838&menu=ultiDatos&idp=1254735976607) |
| Rents | [INE, Rental price index](https://www.ine.es/experimental/ipva/experimental_precios_vivienda_alquiler.htm) · [SERPAVI](https://www.mivau.gob.es/vivienda/alquila-bien-es-tu-derecho/serpavi) |
| Appraised housing value | [Ministry of Housing](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/IOE/operacion.htm?numinv=20007) |

::: {.small .muted}
All INE price indices: [here](https://www.ine.es/dyngs/INEbase/categoria.htm?c=Estadistica_P&cid=1254735976607).
:::

::: notes
For each series, check the geographic level (province or region) and the years available. The INE rental price index is experimental and runs to 2024. For years before the Continuous Population Statistics, use the Continuous Register (Padrón continuo) statistics.
:::

## A possible model (just an example)

::: {.callout-note title="Example"}
Price~pt~ = α + β · Immigration~pt~ + ε~pt~
:::

- *p*: province, *t*: year
- **β > 0**: where more immigrants arrive, housing becomes more expensive

::: {.small .muted}
Only indicative: we will define the model once we have the question and the data.
:::
